step.name: Step 1
step.text: Installing new cabinets can really transform a kitchen, but it's easy to run into snags if you're not careful. One big mistake is skipping those crucial level and plumb checks. You absolutely need to make sure your walls and floors are perfectly aligned before you even think about attaching anything. Another common pitfall is failing to confirm stud locations; you don't want your beautiful new cabinets pulling away from the wall down the line. Folks often don't account for uneven floors or walls, which means everything looks off-kilter. Plus, trying to tighten cabinets together before they're properly aligned? That's a recipe for gaps and an unprofessional look.

step.name: Step 2
step.text: To avoid these issues, always start with meticulous measurements and verification of stud locations. Take the time to mark your layout lines clearly. If your walls or floors aren't perfectly straight, use shims to get everything level and plumb. It's a small step that makes a huge difference in the final outcome. When fastening cabinets, make sure each one is individually aligned and secure before you join them. This attention to detail ensures a seamless and sturdy installation.

step.name: Step 3
step.text: While a basic installation might seem straightforward, if your walls are seriously out of whack or you have complex custom cabinets, it’s often best to call in a professional. They've got the tools and experience to tackle those tricky situations and ensure a perfect fit.
